title: הצבע שהיה יקר מזהב — והחילזון שהסתיר אותו
summary: Tyrian purple from murex sea snails: the gland secretion is nearly colourless — air (enzyme + oxygen) turns it yellow-green and sunlight does the last step to blue and purple (stops at yellow-green in the dark for most species); Friedländer 1909: 12,000 snails → 1.4 g, enough for one garment's trim (≈8,600 snails per gram); Diocletian's price edict 301 CE: purple silk 150,000 denarii/pound vs gold 72,000, purple wool 50,000, a worker 25/day (6,000 days); emperor-only purple, 'born in the purple'; Tel Shikmona (Haifa, ~30 km from Zikhron Ya'akov): largest known Iron Age purple-dye factory (Gilboa & Shalvi, Univ. of Haifa 2023), Phoenician then Kingdom of Israel; Timna purple wool (2021); 6,6'-dibromoindigo = indigo + 2 Br (262 vs 420), Elsner (Shenkar, 1980s) sunlight debromination → blue/tekhelet; Perkin's mauve 1856; maths: ratios, division, g→mg, fractions.
reviewer_verdict: PASS (2 rounds) — nits left: the molecule canvas's colour-name plate covers much of the colour swatch; snail icons are stylised spindle shells; the older standard and advanced (א) share the answer 2,880 (each kid sees only one)
